classification.difficultyReason: Evaluate a quadratic volume model, compare average and instantaneous rates, and interpret when its decreasing flow rate is greatest.

content.prompt: Water is poured into a tank and the volume $V$, in litres, after $t$ seconds is $V=200+80t-2t^2$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the amount of water initially.

children.label: b
children.prompt: If the tank was full in 20 seconds, what is the capacity of the tank?

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the average rate of change during the first 10 seconds and compare it with the instantaneous rate of change after 10 seconds.

answer.short: Average: $60\text{ L/s}$. Instantaneous: $40\text{ L/s}$. The average rate is $20\text{ L/s}$ greater.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}V(10)&=200+80(10)-2(10)^2\\V(10)&=800\text{ L}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Average rate}&=\frac{V(10)-V(0)}{10-0}\\\text{Average rate}&=\frac{800-200}{10}\\\text{Average rate}&=60\text{ L/s}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}V'(t)&=80-4t\\V'(10)&=80-4(10)\\V'(10)&=40\text{ L/s}\end{align*}$$
The average rate over the first 10 seconds is $20\text{ L/s}$ greater than the instantaneous rate after 10 seconds.

children.label: d
children.prompt: When was the flow rate the greatest?

answer.worked:
$$V'(t)=80-4t.$$
The flow rate decreases as $t$ increases, so it is greatest initially, at $t=0\text{ s}$. Its initial value is $80\text{ L/s}$.
